We measured the popup cost three ways. Spawning date took 1.6 to 2.0 ms per row, command substitution took 0.39 ms, and printf -v took 0.014 ms. The older code ran one date exec and about ten subshells per row, so six sessions meant six execs and sixty forks, roughly 35 ms before fzf saw any input. We hoisted date out of the loop so it runs once per invocation, precomputed the colour codes as SGR strings so bash expands them instead of a subshell, and replaced rpad, pill and star with variable assignments. Padding now costs 0.014 ms instead of 0.39 ms. The list command went from 50 ms to 12.8 ms. What remains is two tmux round trips at 3.8 and 4.2 ms, bash startup at 2 ms, the popup sh -c at 2 ms, sort and cut at about 3 ms, and fzf's first paint at about 7 ms.
